- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.3) in recent days, model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots in subsequent days; apply a 1–3 day lag correction, reducing forecast by 1–2% per day.
- Model consistently underestimates mean-reverting periods (e.g., after 68–70 range); add 0.5–1.5% upward bias for 3–5 days if sentiment is neutral or mildly positive.
- For 30-day horizon, model often misses late-period momentum; increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% for last 5–7 days if sentiment is positive or volatile.
- If sentiment is mixed (0.3–0.6) and price is trending, model tends to lag; add 0.5–1.0% bias toward recent price direction for next 3–5 days.
